e-458.knowledge_point: Calculating Indefinite Integrals of Algebraic Functions Using Substitution
e-458.worked_solution:
Let $u = x^2+1.$ Then, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=2x\,⟹\,\frac{1}{2}\text{d}u=x\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

We can now solve the integral in terms of $u,$ and then express our final answer in terms of $x\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {x}^{3}\sqrt{{x}^{2}+1}\,\text{d}x & =\int {x}^{2}\cdot x\sqrt{{x}^{2}+1}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int {x}^{2}\sqrt{{x}^{2}+1}\,\cdot x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int \overset{u-1}{\overset{⏞}{{x}^{2}}}\sqrt{{x}^{2}+1}\cdot \overset{\frac{1}{2}\text{d}u}{\overset{⏞}{x\,\text{d}x}} \\  & =\int (u-1)\sqrt{u}\cdot \frac{1}{2}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\int (u-1){u}^{1/2}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\int ({u}^{3/2}-{u}^{1/2})\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(\frac{2}{5}{u}^{5/2}-\frac{2}{3}{u}^{3/2})+C \\  & =\frac{1}{5}({x}^{2}+1)^{5/2}-\frac{1}{3}({x}^{2}+1)^{3/2}+C \\  & =\frac{1}{5}\sqrt{({x}^{2}+1)^{5}}-\frac{1}{3}\sqrt{({x}^{2}+1)^{3}}+C\end{aligned}
$$

e-457.knowledge_point: Calculating Definite Integrals of Algebraic Functions Using Substitution
e-457.worked_solution:
Let $u=1-2x.$ Then, we have

$$
\dfrac{\textrm d u}{\textrm d x} = -2\quad\Longrightarrow\quad -\dfrac 1 2 \,\textrm d u = \textrm d x.
$$

We also note that $x = \dfrac 1 2 (1-u).$ 

Computing our limits of integration, we get

| **$x$** | $0$ | $1/2$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **$u$** | $1$ | $0$ |

We can now solve the integral using our new variable $u,$ remembering to use the new limits of integration:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1/2}x(1-2x)^{5}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{1}^{0}\frac{1}{2}\cdot (1-u)\cdot {u}^{5}\cdot (-\frac{1}{2})\,\text{d}u \\  & =-\frac{1}{4}{\int }_{1}^{0}(1-u)\cdot {u}^{5}\,\text{d}u \\  & =-\frac{1}{4}{\int }_{1}^{0}({u}^{5}-{u}^{6})\,\text{d}u \\  & =-\frac{1}{4}{(\frac{1}{6}{u}^{6}-\frac{1}{7}{u}^{7})|}_{1}^{0} \\  & =-\frac{1}{4}([0-0]-[\frac{1}{6}-\frac{1}{7}]) \\  & =-\frac{1}{4}(-\frac{1}{42}) \\  & =\frac{1}{168}\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: Let u=x^2-1, so x dx=du/2 and x^2=u+1. Then the integral is (1/2)∫(u+1)u^(1/2) du=(1/5)u^(5/2)+(1/3)u^(3/2)+C, matching option e.

after.name: Question 1
after.worked_solution:
Let $u={x}^{2}-1.$ Then, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=2x\,⟹\,x\,\text{d}x=\frac{\text{d}u}{2}.
$$

We also note that
${x}^{2}=u+1.$

Now we can solve the integral in terms of $u,$ and then express our final answer in terms of $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {x}^{3}\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}\,\text{d}x & =\int {x}^{2}\cdot \sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}\cdot x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int (u+1)\cdot \sqrt{u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\int (u+1){u}^{1/2}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\int ({u}^{3/2}+{u}^{1/2})\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(\frac{2}{5}{u}^{5/2}+\frac{2}{3}{u}^{3/2})+C \\  & =\frac{1}{5}\sqrt{({x}^{2}-1)^{5}}+\frac{1}{3}\sqrt{({x}^{2}-1)^{3}}+C\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Calculating Indefinite Integrals of Algebraic Functions Using Substitution
content.worked_solution:
Let $u={x}^{2}-1.$ Then, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=2x\,⟹\,x\,\text{d}x=\frac{\text{d}u}{2}.
$$

We also note that
${x}^{2}=u+1.$

Now we can solve the integral in terms of $u,$ and then express our final answer in terms of $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {x}^{3}\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}\,\text{d}x & =\int {x}^{2}\cdot \sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}\cdot x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int (u+1)\cdot \sqrt{u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\int (u+1){u}^{1/2}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\int ({u}^{3/2}+{u}^{1/2})\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(\frac{2}{5}{u}^{5/2}+\frac{2}{3}{u}^{3/2})+C \\  & =\frac{1}{5}\sqrt{({x}^{2}-1)^{5}}+\frac{1}{3}\sqrt{({x}^{2}-1)^{3}}+C\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: Let u=3x+1. Then x=(u-1)/3 and dx=du/3, so the integral becomes (1/9)∫(u^(3/2)-u^(1/2)) du=(2/45)u^(5/2)-(2/27)u^(3/2)+C. Substituting back gives option b.

after.name: Question 2
after.worked_solution:
Let $u=3x+1.$ Then, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=3\,⟹\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{3}\text{d}u.
$$

We also note that
$x=\frac{u-1}{3}.$

Now we can solve the integral in terms of $u,$ and then express our final answer in terms of $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x\sqrt{3x+1}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{u-1}{3}\cdot \sqrt{u}\cdot \frac{1}{3}\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{9}\int ({u}^{3/2}-{u}^{1/2})\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{9}(\frac{1}{5/2}{u}^{5/2}-\frac{1}{3/2}{u}^{3/2})+C \\  & =\frac{1}{9}(\frac{2}{5}{u}^{5/2}-\frac{2}{3}{u}^{3/2})+C \\  & =\frac{2}{45}{u}^{5/2}-\frac{2}{27}{u}^{3/2}+C \\  & =\frac{2}{45}\sqrt{(3x+1)^{5}}-\frac{2}{27}\sqrt{(3x+1)^{3}}+C\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Calculating Indefinite Integrals of Algebraic Functions Using Substitution
content.worked_solution:
Let $u=3x+1.$ Then, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=3\,⟹\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{3}\text{d}u.
$$

We also note that
$x=\frac{u-1}{3}.$

Now we can solve the integral in terms of $u,$ and then express our final answer in terms of $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x\sqrt{3x+1}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{u-1}{3}\cdot \sqrt{u}\cdot \frac{1}{3}\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{9}\int ({u}^{3/2}-{u}^{1/2})\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{9}(\frac{1}{5/2}{u}^{5/2}-\frac{1}{3/2}{u}^{3/2})+C \\  & =\frac{1}{9}(\frac{2}{5}{u}^{5/2}-\frac{2}{3}{u}^{3/2})+C \\  & =\frac{2}{45}{u}^{5/2}-\frac{2}{27}{u}^{3/2}+C \\  & =\frac{2}{45}\sqrt{(3x+1)^{5}}-\frac{2}{27}\sqrt{(3x+1)^{3}}+C\end{aligned}
$$

before.html:
Question 3
?

Given that u=x+1, which integral is equivalent to ∫x2x+1dx?

a
∫(u3−2u2+1u)du
b
∫(u3−2u)du
c
∫(u3+1u)du
d
∫(1u−2u)du
e
∫(u3−2u+1u)du
Submit

decision.explanation: Since u=x+1, x=u-1 and dx=du. Thus x^2/sqrt(x+1)=(u-1)^2/sqrt(u)=u^(3/2)-2sqrt(u)+1/sqrt(u), which matches option e.

after.name: Question 3
after.problem: Given that $u=x+1,$ which integral is equivalent to $\int \frac{{x}^{2}}{\sqrt{x+1}}\,\text{d}x?$
after.worked_solution:
Since $u=x+1,$ we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=1\,⟹\,\text{d}u=\text{d}x.
$$

We also note that 
$x=u-1.$

Now we can rewrite the integral in terms of $u:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{{x}^{2}}{\sqrt{x+1}}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{(u-1)^{2}}{\sqrt{u}}\text{d}u \\  & =\int ({u}^{2}-2u+1){u}^{-1/2}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\int ({u}^{3/2}-2{u}^{1/2}+{u}^{-1/2})\,\text{d}u \\  & =\int (\sqrt{{u}^{3}}-2\sqrt{u}+\frac{1}{\sqrt{u}})\,\text{d}u\end{aligned}
$$

Question 3
?

Given that u=x+1, which integral is equivalent to ∫x2x+1dx?

a
∫(u3−2u2+1u)du
b
∫(u3−2u)du
c
∫(u3+1u)du
d
∫(1u−2u)du
e
∫(u3−2u+1u)du
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Since u=x+1, we have dudx=1⟹du=dx.

We also note that x=u−1.

Now we can rewrite the integral in terms of u:

∫x2x+1dx=∫(u−1)2udu=∫(u2−2u+1)u−1/2du=∫(u3/2−2u1/2+u−1/2)du=∫(u3−2u+1u)du

content.knowledge_point: Calculating Indefinite Integrals of Algebraic Functions Using Substitution
content.problem: Given that $u=x+1,$ which integral is equivalent to $\int \frac{{x}^{2}}{\sqrt{x+1}}\,\text{d}x?$
content.worked_solution:
Since $u=x+1,$ we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=1\,⟹\,\text{d}u=\text{d}x.
$$

We also note that 
$x=u-1.$

Now we can rewrite the integral in terms of $u:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{{x}^{2}}{\sqrt{x+1}}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{(u-1)^{2}}{\sqrt{u}}\text{d}u \\  & =\int ({u}^{2}-2u+1){u}^{-1/2}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\int ({u}^{3/2}-2{u}^{1/2}+{u}^{-1/2})\,\text{d}u \\  & =\int (\sqrt{{u}^{3}}-2\sqrt{u}+\frac{1}{\sqrt{u}})\,\text{d}u\end{aligned}
$$

before.html:
Question 4
?

Calculate the integral of (2x+1)4−x.

a
−6(4−x)3+45(4−x)5+C
b
6(2x+1)3−15(2x+1)5+C
c
34−x3−45(4−x)3+C
d
−(4−x)3+15(4−x)5+C
e
−8(2x+1)3+45(2x+1)3+C
Submit

decision.explanation: Let u=4-x, so dx=-du and 2x+1=9-2u. The integral becomes ∫(2u^(3/2)-9u^(1/2)) du=(4/5)u^(5/2)-6u^(3/2)+C. Substituting back matches option a.

after.name: Question 4
after.worked_solution:
Let $u=4-x.$ Then, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=-1\,⟹\,\text{d}x=-\text{d}u.
$$

We also note that
$x=4-u.$

Now we can solve the integral in terms of $u,$ and then express our final answer in terms of $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (2x+1)\sqrt{4-x}\,\text{d}x & =\int (2(4-u)+1)\sqrt{u}(-\text{d}u) \\  & =-\int (9-2u)\sqrt{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =-\int (9{u}^{1/2}-2{u}^{3/2})\text{d}u \\  & =-(6{u}^{3/2}-\frac{4}{5}{u}^{5/2})+C \\  & =-6\sqrt{(4-x)^{3}}+\frac{4}{5}\sqrt{(4-x)^{5}}+C\end{aligned}
$$

Question 4
?

Calculate the integral of (2x+1)4−x.

a
−6(4−x)3+45(4−x)5+C
b
6(2x+1)3−15(2x+1)5+C
c
34−x3−45(4−x)3+C
d
−(4−x)3+15(4−x)5+C
e
−8(2x+1)3+45(2x+1)3+C
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Let u=4−x. Then, we have dudx=−1⟹dx=−du.

We also note that x=4−u.

Now we can solve the integral in terms of u, and then express our final answer in terms of x:

∫(2x+1)4−xdx=∫(2(4−u)+1)u(−du)=−∫(9−2u)udu=−∫(9u1/2−2u3/2)du=−(6u3/2−45u5/2)+C=−6(4−x)3+45(4−x)5+C

verification.explanation: The worked solution confirms option a: substituting u=4-x gives -∫(9u^(1/2)-2u^(3/2)) du=-6u^(3/2)+(4/5)u^(5/2)+C. Differentiating the result gives [9-2(4-x)]sqrt(4-x)=(2x+1)sqrt(4-x).

content.knowledge_point: Calculating Indefinite Integrals of Algebraic Functions Using Substitution
content.worked_solution:
Let $u=4-x.$ Then, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=-1\,⟹\,\text{d}x=-\text{d}u.
$$

We also note that
$x=4-u.$

Now we can solve the integral in terms of $u,$ and then express our final answer in terms of $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (2x+1)\sqrt{4-x}\,\text{d}x & =\int (2(4-u)+1)\sqrt{u}(-\text{d}u) \\  & =-\int (9-2u)\sqrt{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =-\int (9{u}^{1/2}-2{u}^{3/2})\text{d}u \\  & =-(6{u}^{3/2}-\frac{4}{5}{u}^{5/2})+C \\  & =-6\sqrt{(4-x)^{3}}+\frac{4}{5}\sqrt{(4-x)^{5}}+C\end{aligned}
$$

Question 5
?

Find the integral of xx−2.

a
23x3+12x+C
b
25(x−2)3+52(x−2)5+C
c
25(x−2)5+43(x−2)3+C
d
25x5+12x+C
e
23(x−2)3+13x−2+C
Submit

decision.explanation: Let u=x-2, so x=u+2 and dx=du. Then ∫x√(x-2) dx=∫(u^(3/2)+2u^(1/2)) du=(2/5)u^(5/2)+(4/3)u^(3/2)+C, matching option c.

after.name: Question 5
after.worked_solution:
Let $u=x-2.$ Then, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=1\,⟹\,\text{d}x=\text{d}u.
$$

We also note that
$x=u+2.$

Now we can solve the integral in terms of $u,$ and then express our final answer in terms of $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x\sqrt{x-2}\,\text{d}x & =\int (u+2)\sqrt{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\int {u}^{3/2}+2{u}^{1/2}\,\text{d}u \\  & =(\frac{2}{5}{u}^{5/2}+\frac{4}{3}{u}^{3/2})+C \\  & =\frac{2}{5}\sqrt{(x-2)^{5}}+\frac{4}{3}\sqrt{(x-2)^{3}}+C\end{aligned}
$$

Question 5
?

Find the integral of xx−2.

a
23x3+12x+C
b
25(x−2)3+52(x−2)5+C
c
25(x−2)5+43(x−2)3+C
d
25x5+12x+C
e
23(x−2)3+13x−2+C
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Let u=x−2. Then, we have dudx=1⟹dx=du.

after.worked_solution:
Let $u=6x+6.$ Then, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=6\,⟹\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{6}\text{d}u.
$$

We also note that $x=\frac{1}{6}(u-6).$ 

Computing our limits of integration, we get

| **$x$** | $-1$ | $1/3$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **$u$** | $0$ | $8$ |

We can now solve the integral using our new variable $u,$ remembering to use the new limits of integration:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-1}^{1/3}\frac{7}{4}x\sqrt[3]{6x+6}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{8}\frac{7}{4}\cdot \frac{1}{6}(u-6)\cdot {u}^{1/3}\cdot \frac{1}{6}\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{7}{144}{\int }_{0}^{8}({u}^{4/3}-6{u}^{1/3})\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{7}{144}{(\frac{1}{(7/3)}{u}^{7/3}-6\cdot \frac{1}{(4/3)}{u}^{4/3})|}_{0}^{8} \\  & =\frac{7}{144}{(\frac{3}{7}{u}^{7/3}-\frac{9}{2}{u}^{4/3})|}_{0}^{8} \\  & =\frac{7}{144}[(\frac{3}{7}\cdot {8}^{7/3}-\frac{9}{2}\cdot {8}^{4/3})-(\frac{3}{7}\cdot {0}^{7/3}-\frac{9}{2}\cdot {0}^{4/3})] \\  & =\frac{7}{144}(\frac{384}{7}-72) \\  & =\frac{7}{144}\cdot (-\frac{120}{7}) \\  & =-\frac{5}{6}\end{aligned}
$$

before.html:
Question 7
?

Given that u=2x−1, which integral is equivalent to ∫13x2x−1dx?

a
14∫15udu
b
12∫13udu
c
14∫15(u3/2+u1/2)du
d
12∫15(u1/2+u−1/2)du
e
12∫13(u3/2+u1/2)du
Submit

decision.explanation: With u=2x-1, x=(u+1)/2 and dx=du/2. The limits x=1 and x=3 become u=1 and u=5. Thus the integral becomes (1/4)∫₁⁵(u^(3/2)+u^(1/2)) du, matching option c.

after.name: Question 7
after.problem: Given that $u=2x-1$, which integral is equivalent to ${\int }_{1}^{3}x\sqrt{2x-1}\,\text{d}x?$
after.worked_solution:
Since $u=2x-1$, then we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=2\,⟹\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{2}\text{d}u.
$$

We also note that $x=\frac{u+1}{2}.$ 

Computing our limits of integration, we get

| **$x$** | $1$ | $3$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **$u$** | $1$ | $5$ |

We can now solve the integral using our new variable $u,$ remembering to use the new limits of integration:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{3}x\sqrt{2x-1}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{1}^{5}\frac{u+1}{2}\cdot \sqrt{u}\cdot \frac{1}{2}\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{4}{\int }_{1}^{5}(u+1){u}^{1/2}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{4}{\int }_{1}^{5}({u}^{3/2}+{u}^{1/2})\text{d}u\end{aligned}
$$

Since u=2x−1, then we have dudx=2⟹dx=12du.

We also note that x=u+12.

Computing our limits of integration, we get

x 1 3

∫13x2x−1dx=∫15u+12⋅u⋅12du=14∫15(u+1)u1/2du=14∫15(u3/2+u1/2)du

content.knowledge_point: Calculating Definite Integrals of Algebraic Functions Using Substitution
content.problem: Given that $u=2x-1$, which integral is equivalent to ${\int }_{1}^{3}x\sqrt{2x-1}\,\text{d}x?$
content.worked_solution:
Since $u=2x-1$, then we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=2\,⟹\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{2}\text{d}u.
$$

We also note that $x=\frac{u+1}{2}.$ 

Computing our limits of integration, we get

| **$x$** | $1$ | $3$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **$u$** | $1$ | $5$ |

We can now solve the integral using our new variable $u,$ remembering to use the new limits of integration:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{3}x\sqrt{2x-1}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{1}^{5}\frac{u+1}{2}\cdot \sqrt{u}\cdot \frac{1}{2}\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{4}{\int }_{1}^{5}(u+1){u}^{1/2}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{4}{\int }_{1}^{5}({u}^{3/2}+{u}^{1/2})\text{d}u\end{aligned}
$$

after.worked_solution:
Let $u=x+2.$ Then, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=1\,⟹\,\text{d}x=\text{d}u.
$$

We also note that $x=u-2.$

Computing our limits of integration, we get

| **$x$** | $-2$ | $0$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **$u$** | $0$ | $2$ |

We can now solve the integral using our new variable $u,$ remembering to use the new limits of integration:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-2}^{0}x{(x+2)}^{3}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{2}(u-2){u}^{3}\,\text{d}u \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}({u}^{4}-2{u}^{3})\,\text{d}u \\  & ={(\frac{1}{5}{u}^{5}-2\cdot \frac{1}{4}{u}^{4})|}_{0}^{2} \\  & ={(\frac{1}{5}{u}^{5}-\frac{1}{2}{u}^{4})|}_{0}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{5}({2}^{5}-{0}^{5})-\frac{1}{2}({2}^{4}-{0}^{4}) \\  & =\frac{1}{5}(32-0)-\frac{1}{2}(16-0) \\  & =\frac{32}{5}-8 \\  & =-\frac{8}{5}\end{aligned}
$$
